name: After recital 2
title: REPORT on the amended proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive 1999/62/EC, Council Directive 1999/37/EC and Directive (EU) 2019/520 as regards the CO2 emission class of heavy-duty vehicles with trailers and clarifying and simplifying certain provisions
part_text: (2a) While improving the energy efficiency of trailers may contribute to reducing fuel consumption and emissions, such measures should not be considered in isolation from their economic and operational consequences for the road freight transport sector. The additional costs associated with mandatory efficiency requirements, CO₂-based road charging and other measures introduced under the Union’s climate policy framework, including the European Green Deal, may place a disproportionate burden on transport operators, manufacturers and consumers, particularly in Member States where road transport is essential for domestic and cross-border trade. The introduction of further regulatory or financial incentives for energy-efficient trailers should therefore be subject to a thorough assessment of their actual benefits, economic impact and technological feasibility, while respecting the principle of proportionality and the competence of Member States to determine measures appropriate to their national economic and transport circumstances.
